title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: exclude specific domains from web grounding
summary: Hold for a control-reference correction: the web-search UI link opens a generic Cloud Policy guide that does not document the Allow web search in Copilot setting. The route itself is supported across the cited Microsoft pages, and the domain-exclusion and DLP commands are documented. Two smaller corrections would complete the Purview route and identify the Graph setting property in the table note.

claims.where: front matter: products; title; What's changing
claims.claim: The roadmap plans domain exclusion for web grounding in Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: This feature will allow admins to specify a limited set of sites to exclude from web grounding in M365 Copilot and Copilot Chat #copilotcontrolsystem

claims.claim: The roadmap status is rolling out.
claims.quote: "status": "Rolling out", "statusKey": "rolling-out"

claims.claim: The roadmap target is September CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "September CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap provides no preview date.
claims.quote: "previewDate": null

claims.claim: The roadmap release phase is General Availability.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": [ "General Availability" ]

claims.claim: The roadmap lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant), not government clouds.
claims.quote: "clouds": [ "Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)" ]

claims.claim: The roadmap lists Desktop and Web.
claims.quote: "platforms": [ "Desktop", "Web" ]

claims.claim: The roadmap modification timestamp is 2026-09-01T23:00:02.
Administrators can exclude up to 1,000 sites from Copilot and Copilot Chat web grounding.
claims.quote: By using domain exclusion, you can specify up to 1,000 sites to exclude from web grounding in Microsoft Copilot and Copilot Chat through a PowerShell script.

claims.claim: The configuration supports up to two levels of subdomains.
claims.quote: Currently, the domain exclusion configuration supports up to two levels of subdomains.

claims.claim: Tenant domain exclusions are managed through ConfigureTenantDomainExclusions.ps1.
claims.quote: To manage the Copilot domain exclusion configuration for your tenant, use the ConfigureTenantDomainExclusions.ps1 PowerShell script.

claims.claim: The script download is at aka.ms/Copilot/DomainExclusionScript.
claims.quote: Download it at https://aka.ms/Copilot/DomainExclusionScript.

claims.claim: The script can retrieve the current exclusion configuration and export it to CSV.
claims.quote: Get the current domain exclusion configuration and export to CSV

claims.claim: The script can update the exclusion configuration from CSV.
claims.quote: Update an existing domain exclusion configuration from CSV file

claims.claim: The script can delete the exclusion configuration.
claims.quote: Delete the current domain exclusion configuration

claims.claim: The script can generate a template CSV.
claims.quote: Generate a template CSV file for domain exclusions

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment
claims.claim: Domain exclusions currently filter web page results only.
claims.quote: Currently, domain exclusions support filtering on web page results only.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Results from other answer verticals, such as news, might still cite excluded sites.
claims.quote: Results from other answer verticals, such as news, might still be cited.

claims.claim: Domain exclusion is admin-opt-in: default settings contain no exclusion configuration, and an administrator runs the script to opt in.
claims.quote: Default settings don't include the domain exclusion configuration. Opt in to use the feature by running the PowerShell script.

claims.claim: Cowork uses the organization's domain exclusion policy.
claims.quote: Cowork uses your organization's domain exclusion policies, including exclusions for specific domains.

claims.claim: The script requires signing in as a Search Administrator or Global Administrator.
claims.quote: Sign in as a Search Administrator or Global Administrator.

claims.claim: The script needs the Az.Accounts PowerShell module.
claims.quote: Az.Accounts PowerShell module (the ConfigureTenantDomainExclusions.ps1 script installs the module automatically if it's missing).

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented an admin UI for tenant domain exclusions as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot domain exclusion admin center UI; opened learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/domain-exclusion and copilot/implement/configure-copilot-admin-center. Both document no domain-exclusion UI; search results document the script.

claims.claim: ConfigureTenantDomainExclusions.ps1 -Create -FromFile <csv> creates the tenant exclusion configuration from CSV.
claims.quote: Create your domain exclusion configuration from a CSV file: .\ConfigureTenantDomainExclusions.ps1 -Create -FromFile "input.csv"

claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 Apps admin center route through Customization, Policy Management, Policy configurations, Create and the wizard reaches Allow web search in Copilot.
claims.quote: Under Customization, select Policy Management. On the Policy configurations page, select Create. On the Configure Settings page, select the policies that you want to include in the policy configuration.

claims.where: controls[1].ui: docs; rendered table: web search UI Learn link
claims.claim: The UI row's linked Cloud Policy overview documents the control-specific final step, Allow web search in Copilot.
claims.quote: Searched: Allow web search in Copilot in the full Cloud Policy overview; absent. Opened learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/manage-public-web-access, which names the setting and Cloud Policy service. The route is supported, but the row's docs page lacks its control-specific step.
claims.fix: Replace controls[1].ui.docs and the matching rendered UI Learn link with https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/manage-public-web-access#it-admin-control-for-both-microsoft-copilot-and-microsoft-copilot-chat. Keep the existing path and the Cloud Policy overview in sources: that overview supplies the wizard route, while this page supplies the control-specific step.

claims.claim: Cloud Policy UI configurations can target the tenant's users or specific groups.
claims.quote: On the Choose the scope page, determine whether the policy configuration applies to all users, specific groups, or to users who anonymously access documents using Office for the web.

claims.claim: Allow web search in Copilot governs web-search access in both Copilot and Copilot Chat through Cloud Policy.
claims.quote: The primary way that IT admins can control access to web search is by using the Allow web search in Copilot policy, which is available only in Cloud Policy service for Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: The policy can enable web search in both Copilot and Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: Enabled in Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Chat

claims.claim: The policy can disable web search in both Copilot and Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: Disabled in Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Chat

claims.claim: The policy can disable web search in Work mode while enabling it in Web mode and Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: Disabled in Microsoft Copilot Work mode; Enabled in Microsoft Copilot Web mode and Microsoft Copilot Chat

claims.claim: Users retain a personal web-search toggle when web search is allowed, but cannot enable web search when the administrator disables it.
claims.quote: If the IT admin turns off web search, the Web content toggle is turned off and appears dimmed. Users can't turn on the toggle to use web search.

claims.claim: POST /beta/admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors can set web-search policy using an applyOnce monitor and an allowwebsearch baseline.
claims.quote: Create a new configurationMonitor object that runs periodically in the background at a scheduled frequency to detect configuration drift in monitorOnly mode, or applies a desired-state baseline once in applyOnce mode.
claims.fix: Append to controls[1].note and its rendered copy: "Request body: mode = applyOnce; baseline.resources uses resourceType microsoft.copilot.allowwebsearch, resourceVersion 1, and properties.value as a string (0 enables, 1 disables, 2 disables Work mode only)." These properties are documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/utcm-copilot-resources#allowwebsearch-resource-type and already appear in the prose.

claims.claim: Graph Tenant Configuration Management applyOnce is in preview through Microsoft Graph beta.
claims.quote: These capabilities are available in preview through Microsoft Graph beta.

claims.claim: TCM supports this Copilot policy only at tenant level.
claims.quote: TCM supports these settings only in tenant-level policies in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center.

claims.claim: TCM operations fail for the resource if its setting is configured in a group-level policy.
claims.quote: Before using TCM, ensure that the target setting isn't configured in any group-level policy in that admin center. If it is, monitoring, snapshots, remediation, and applyOnce fail for that resource.

claims.claim: AI Administrator is the least-privileged signed-in user role for applying the web-search resource.
claims.quote: For remediation and applyOnce, AI Administrator is the least-privileged Microsoft Entra role for the signed-in user. This role requirement applies to the user, not to the TCM service principal.

claims.claim: The Graph monitor uses applyOnce mode to apply the desired-state baseline.
claims.quote: An active applyOnce monitor runs in the background on behalf of the signed-in administrator and then becomes inactive.

claims.claim: The baseline resourceType is microsoft.copilot.allowwebsearch.
claims.quote: "resourceType": "microsoft.copilot.allowwebsearch"

claims.claim: The baseline resourceVersion is 1.
claims.quote: "resourceVersion": 1

claims.claim: The setting is specified through properties.value as a string.
claims.quote: The value property is a string, not a Boolean or a number. Its meaning varies by setting.

claims.claim: The string value 0 enables web search in Copilot and Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: 0 enables it in Microsoft 365 Copilot and Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: The string value 1 disables web search in both experiences.
claims.quote: 1 disables it in both.

claims.claim: The string value 2 disables Work-mode web search while enabling Web-mode and Copilot Chat web search.
claims.quote: 2 disables it in Microsoft 365 Copilot Work mode while enabling it in Microsoft 365 Copilot Web mode and Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: The Purview route through Data Loss Prevention, Policies, + Create policy, Custom, Custom policy and Locations reaches the Copilot policy location.
claims.quote: Go to Data Loss Prevention > Policies and select + Create policy. Select the Custom template, then Custom policy. On the Locations page, set the Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork location to on.
claims.fix: Extend controls[2].ui.path and its rendered copy to "Data Loss Prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Custom > Custom policy > Locations > Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork > rule > Content contains > Sensitive information types > Prevent Copilot from processing content > Performing Web Searches". The cited page gives these remaining steps; the existing path stops at the location, not the web-search action.

claims.claim: New-DlpComplianceRule -Policy <policy> -RestrictWebGrounding $true creates a rule in the identified policy that blocks web grounding.
claims.quote: The Policy parameter specifies the existing DLP policy that contains the new DLP rule. The RestrictWebGrounding parameter specifies an action for the DLP rule that blocks web grounding. Valid values are: $true: Web grounding is blocked.

claims.claim: New-DlpComplianceRule is available in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.claim: The web-search DLP rule uses Content contains > Sensitive information types as its condition.
claims.quote: Add a rule with the Content contains > Sensitive information types condition and choose the SITs you want to detect.

claims.claim: The DLP action is Prevent Copilot from processing content > Performing Web Searches.
claims.quote: In the same rule, set the action to Prevent Copilot from processing content > Performing Web Searches.

claims.claim: Purview DLP can block external web search for a Copilot or Copilot Chat prompt that matches configured sensitive information types.
claims.quote: When a user prompt contains the configured SITs, Copilot and Cowork block external web search as a grounding source and continue to generate the response using allowed internal Microsoft 365 data sources.

claims.claim: The domain-exclusion option is classified as included under the product-level licensing, with no separately published feature entitlement.
claims.quote: Copilot Chat (Basic) is the standalone baseline experience included with eligible Microsoft 365 licenses.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Copilot Chat (Basic) is included with eligible Microsoft 365 licenses.
claims.quote: Copilot Chat (Basic) is the standalone baseline experience included with eligible Microsoft 365 licenses.

claims.claim: The full Copilot experience uses the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license.
claims.quote: You have the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license with access to the full experience of Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote.

claims.quote: Searched: Copilot domain exclusion licensing pricing meter. Opened learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/domain-exclusion, copilot/plan/pay-as-you-go-overview and copilot/plan/pay-as-you-go-meters; documented agent meters do not meter domain-exclusion configuration.

claims.claim: Domain-result filtering does not replace the enabled web-search flow that sends generated queries to Bing.
claims.quote: Based on these terms, Copilot generates a search query that it sends to the Bing search service asking for more information.

claims.claim: A generated web-search query consists of a few words informed by the user's prompt.
claims.quote: This generated search query is different from the user's original prompt-it consists of a few words informed by the user's prompt.

claims.claim: Generated search queries do not contain entire Microsoft 365 files.
claims.quote: The following information isn't included in the generated search query sent to the Bing search service: Entire Microsoft 365 files (for example, emails or documents) or files uploaded into Copilot

claims.claim: A search query can be informed by organizational document content.
claims.quote: When the user explicitly references a specific document in their prompt. Copilot reasons over this document and identifies "clean energy policy" as a major theme. "Clean energy policy" is added to the generated search query sent to the Bing search service (the document itself isn't included).

claims.claim: A generated query can contain the manager's name obtained from Microsoft 365 data.
claims.quote: Copilot finds the name of the user's manager from Microsoft 365 data. It then generates a Bing search query based on their name to see what information about them is available on the web.

claims.claim: A very short prompt can itself be sent as the generated search query.
claims.quote: The user's entire prompt, unless the prompt is very short (for example, "local weather")

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented domain-exclusion user messaging as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: domain exclusion user notification; Copilot domain exclusion admin UI user notification message wildcard TLD. Opened learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/domain-exclusion and copilot/implement/configure-copilot-admin-center; no feature-specific user messaging found.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not described wildcard-style blocking of whole TLDs for this Copilot control.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot domain exclusion admin UI user notification message wildcard TLD. Read learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/domain-exclusion including CSV format and limitations; it specifies valid domains or URLs, not whole-TLD wildcard exclusion.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented the interaction between tenant domain exclusions and a declarative agent scoped to an excluded site.
claims.quote: Searched: domain exclusion declarative scoped. Read learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/domain-exclusion and microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/knowledge-sources, including Web and scoped web search; results discuss web-search disabling, not this exclusion interaction.
